newsitem.title: UK: British, German stocks fall on fresh rate worries.
newsitem.headline: British, German stocks fall on fresh rate worries.

text.p: Key European bourses fell after touching peaks on Tuesday on renewed doubts about U.S. interest rates and after a poor start on Wall Street eclipsed its record-breaking run.

London and Frankurt soared briefly to new highs, cheered by a brief positive opening on Wall Street, then quickly lost ground as the tide in New York changed and stocks plunged 0.6 percent in the first hour.
Wall Street's early gains were wiped out after comments by a senior central bank Federal Reserve official led the market to believe interest rates might be raised.

The unidentified official told Reuters eight of 12 Fed banks had requested an increase in the five percent discount rate and of the eight banks, three requested a raise in interest rates of 50 basis points.
The change in mood came after London and Frankfurt had both opened strongly, powered by Monday's record close on Wall Street where hopes had grown that U.S. interest rates would remain unchanged.

But the European gains were fragile even though Monday's stampede on Wall Street had driven London's FTSE 100 index to a trading peak of 3,986.7 points. By mid-afternoon, the jitters had set in and London was down 0.25 percent.
Another indication of the cautious mood was that trade volumes were thin.

"We had expected the market to go well this morning but there was just no business there at all. It's very frustrating. People seem to be waiting for a fall on Wall Street," a London equities dealer said.

Frankfurt also fell after touching a new high in opening deals on the computerised IBIS index. Floor trading ended down 1.79 points on the DAX index after closing at a record high of 2,629.87 on Monday.
"Some market players clearly do not trust recent developments too much, there is a degree of scepticism out there," a trader said.

The European markets ran out of steam by mid-morning when doubts took hold about the durability of Wall Street's run and the fresh doubts arose about interest rates in the influential American economy.

The London market was also hesitating at a psychologically-important crossroads as investors speculated what lay beyond the key 4,000 point level. Some analysts predicted a heavy round of profit-taking beyond that level.
"The problem is, we've reached the edge of the map and people are sitting down to think, what next?" one dealer said.
French shares too were retreating into negative territory on the back of Wall Street's drop and renewed concerns over a possible rate increase in the United States, dealers said.
In Milan, shares in Olivetti crashed to a new low in a wave of panic selling as the company scrambled to answer a battery of fresh questions from market regulators about the state of its finances.

The dollar strengthened slightly against after the Fed official's remarks about interest rates. An increase in U.S. interest rates would tend to make the dollar more attractive to foreign exchange dealers.

Forex markets were also analysing the latest U.S. economic figures which showed total output by U.S. mines, factories and utilities increased strongly in August, partly because of a surge in electricity output.

"It came in a touch stronger than market expectations," said Dan Seto, senior economist at The Nikko Securities Co. International Inc. "Overall, the manufacturing sector is crawling out of the doldrums that it had been stuck in for such a long time."
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5142 marks and 110.20 yen compared with late Monday's 1.5105 marks and 110.13 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 10.4 at 3,966.8.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 9.32 points at 2,076.87.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index closed down 1.79 points at 2,628.08.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $383.45 compared with $382.70 at the London close on Monday. Silver was at $5.08, up three cents.
